rationale: The race data shows the current candidate performs excellently on the oval and s-bend tracks, completing them with low rms error and no line loss events. However, it fails to complete the slalom track, going off track early with high rms error and steering oscillation. The slalom track is more challenging with sharper turns, requiring better control and stability. The feedback suggested reducing base_speed to 1.0 if stalls or line loss are high, and tuning PID gains to reduce steering oscillation by lowering kp and kd. The slalom failures indicate the robot is too fast and oversteering in tight curves. Therefore, I reduce base_speed from 1.2 to 1.0 to improve stability and reduce overshoot. I also reduce kp from 8 to 6 and kd from 3 to 2 to soften steering response and reduce oscillations. I increase ki from 0.5 to 1.0 to improve steady-state error correction, helping the robot maintain line tracking in curves. The geometry remains unchanged as it is well balanced and stable. I keep the sensor layout and weights the same, as they provide good line detection coverage. I continue to request the full set of observations to monitor completion, progress, errors, line loss, and control metrics. I expect these changes to improve slalom track completion by reducing overshoot and oscillations, while maintaining good performance on other tracks.
